xrefdescription.para: Request metric tracking Adapter tracks total, successful, and failed request counts
Queue depth tracking Adapter tracks current queue depth
Response headers include processing metadata Responses include X-Processing-Time-Ms header for observability
Session count tracking Adapter tracks number of active sessions

Queue size limit enforcement Adapter rejects requests when queue is at capacity. Uses a small-limit variant (kMaxQueueSize = 3) so concurrent threads can fill the queue reliably without launching thousands of threads.

Session limit enforcement Adapter rejects requests when the active-session limit is reached. Uses a small-limit variant (kMaxActiveSessions = 3) so concurrent threads can exhaust the session budget without thousands of goroutines.
Memory footprint remains bounded Adapter maintains bounded memory usage even with many metrics tracked
Thread-safe metric updates Multiple threads updating metrics concurrently produces consistent results
Concurrent access doesn't cause data corruption Adapter remains functional with concurrent reads and writes to metrics
Consistent error handling under concurrent load Errors are handled consistently when multiple threads make requests
Observability doesn't impact request performance Adding observability infrastructure doesn't significantly impact latency
Tracing metadata is non-intrusive Adding tracing IDs doesn't prevent successful request processing
